words.def: Not alive, or not working because there is no power.
words.note: Say my phone is dead when its battery has run out. Dead can also describe someone who is very tired.

ex.en: My phone is dead. Can I borrow yours?
ex.ar: تلفوني طفا. واش نقدر نستعمل تلفونك؟

col.en: My laptop won't turn on. It has a *dead* battery.
I'm *dead* tired after work.
We followed the road, but it was a *dead* end.
Sorry, I couldn't call you. My phone was *dead*.

words.def: A device that makes bright colours and loud sounds when it explodes in the sky.
words.note: People usually say fireworks when talking about a show or celebration, even when referring to the activity as a whole.

ex.en: We watched the fireworks last night.

col.en: People *set off fireworks* on New Year's Eve.
We watched a beautiful *fireworks display*.
I heard *fireworks going off* outside.

words.def: An object that makes a ringing sound, often to get someone's attention.

ex.en: Someone is ringing the bell. Can you open the door?
ex.ar: شي واحد كيضرب الجرس. واش تقدر تحل الباب؟

col.en: Someone is *ringing the bell*. Can you open the door?
The *doorbell rang* while I was sleeping.
His name *rings a bell*, but I can't remember where I met him.
An alarm *bell went off* in the building.

words.def: To say or write the letters of a word in the correct order.
words.note: Say How do you spell it? when asking about the letters of a word.

ex.en: Could you spell your last name, please?
ex.ar: واش ممكن تتهجّى النسب ديالك، عافاك؟

col.en: Could you *spell your name*, please?
How do you *spell* your first name?
I don't understand. Can you *spell it out* for me?
This decision could *spell trouble* for the company.

words.def: Pleasant, enjoyable, or kind and friendly.

ex.en: It was really nice to meet you.

col.en: Hi, I'm Adam. *Nice to meet you*.

col.p_ar: هادي منك زوينة / هادشي لطف منك
col.en: Thanks for helping me. That's really *nice* of you.
Thanks for calling. *Have a nice day*!
This is a *nice place to live*.

words.def: What people use to buy things and pay for services.
words.note: Money is usually uncountable. Say much money, not many money.

ex.en: I'm trying to save money for a new laptop.
ex.ar: كنحاول نجمع الفلوس باش نشري حاسوب جديد.

col.en: I want to *make money* online.
I'm trying to *save money* for a new laptop.
I don't like spending *money on* things I don't need.
We *ran out of money* before the end of the month.

words.note: Say every day or daily, not every daily. Daily is more common in writing and work contexts.

ex.en: I check my emails every day.

col.en: I want to improve my *daily routine*.
I check my emails *on a daily basis*.
These are my *daily tasks* at work.
Please send me a *daily update* on the project.

words.def: How tall someone or something is, measured from bottom to top.
words.note: Use height for the measurement from bottom to top. Use tall to describe a person's or object's height.

col.en: What's your *height*? I need it for the form.
The *height of the building* is 30 metres.
The drone was flying *at a height of* 10 metres.
The form asks for your *height and weight*.

words.def: How wide something is, measured from one side to the other.
words.note: Height is measured from bottom to top, while width is measured from side to side.

ex.en: What's the width of this table?

col.en: What's the *width of this table*?
You can change the *height and width* of the image.
Make the image *full width*.
The box has a *width of 20 centimetres*.

words.def: A small ball of air in a liquid or soap. As a verb, to form or produce bubbles.

ex.en: The children were blowing bubbles in the garden.
ex.ar: الدراري كانو كينفخو فقاعات الصابون فالجنينة.

col.en: The children love to *blow bubbles*.
Be careful not to *burst the bubbles*.
The water started to *bubble up*.

col.p_ar: يحطم ليه الأمل / يفيقو من الوهم
col.en: I hate to *burst your bubble*, but the shop is already closed.

texts.title: Text 1 – A night with friends
texts.en: Last night, I went to a party with some friends. It was a *nice|nice* place to celebrate, and everyone was happy. At midnight, people started to *set off fireworks|firework* outside. We watched a beautiful *fireworks display|firework* from the balcony. Suddenly, *the doorbell rang|bell*, and someone came to visit us. His name *rang a bell|bell*, but I couldn't remember where I had met him. He asked me to *spell my name|spell*, so I did. Then we talked about our jobs and how we wanted to *make money|money* online. He was trying to *save money|money* because he wanted to buy a new laptop. I told him I was doing the same thing. We also talked about our *daily routines|daily* and the importance of learning new skills *on a daily basis|daily*. Later, we measured the room to change its design. We needed to know *the height and width|height* of the windows. One window had a *width of 120 centimetres|width*. Outside, the children were trying to *blow bubbles|bubble* with soap. Some bubbles started to *bubble up|bubble* in the water. By the time I got home, I was *dead tired|dead*. Unfortunately, *my phone was dead|dead*, too. I couldn't call anyone, so I went straight to bed.
